#### Board rules

Exactly three distinct supported aids/team, once per match; eligible unresolved/unrevealed MAIN-phase only, no unavailable effect consumption. New rules pin configured main time(default30s) then one10s steal phase; host selects an eligible non-main team for its attempt, expiry without answer gives no points. A phase-eligible attempt must be recorded before reveal, then host may adjudicate it; old E1/E2 reveal-first rules remain compatible for those pinned versions. Shared-correct awards enumerate eligible teams explicitly. No late grace; public reveal ends guessing. TRAP transfer is a distinct at-most10s eligibility window, never a second extended MAIN clock.

| Aid | Adopted successor effect |
| --- | --- |
| PHONE_A_FRIEND | Suspend timing with retained remaining duration; server60s assistance, early/automatic end resumes once. Explicit change from legacy continuing clock. |
| DOUBLE_ANSWER | Two recorded attempts within phase deadline; first incorrect preserves one, second exhausts eligibility; correct resolves once without extra base points. |
| MORE_HINT | Ordinary hint reveals first pinned hint only; aid reveals next unrevealed hint, missing next rejects. Explicit change from free unlimited legacy hints. |
| TRAP | Next team in immutable order gets eligibility until min(current deadline,now+10s); original team cannot answer during transfer. |
| PICK_ANSWERER | Persist server-selected roster player and bind attribution; no claim to enforce who physically speaks. |
| STEAL_POINTS | min(pinned question value,max(0,highest opponent score)), stable team-order tie break; zero transfer rejects without consuming. |
| DOUBLE_POINTS | Arm consuming team's single correct award at2× pinned value; other shared-correct teams get ordinary award. Transfer does not move the bonus. |

**Compatibility:** DOUBLE_ANSWER/PICK_ANSWERER/DOUBLE_POINTS combine; MORE_HINT and STEAL_POINTS may combine with them during running play. Steal transfer never doubles. PHONE may suspend those three armed effects; while paused no aid/attempt/hint/score action, expiry/end restores retained state. TRAP requires no earlier aid consumed on this question, prevents further aids there; first ordinary hint is not aid consumption. Reuse/revealed/terminal/STEAL-phase aid use rejects. Persist this rules version/matrix, do not infer combinations in client UI.

#### Standalone list rules

Select three distinct aids; each once per genuine question, reset only NEXT_ROUND. HINT reveals first Unicode grapheme of highest-value hidden nontrap item, stable order tie break, unavailable rejects. PASS transfers/reset-turn, overall question cap unchanged. FREEZE pauses both timers with stored remaining durations until host resume. DOUBLE gives two consecutive attempts: first incorrect does not transfer, second incorrect does; correct retains normal award/reset, trap terminates allowance/transfers immediately. PHONE is the60s assistance pause. One ordinary incorrect attempt without DOUBLE transfers turn. HINT combines with DOUBLE; FREEZE/PHONE may suspend its remaining attempts but cannot overlap each other; no judgement/new aid while paused. PASS rejects with DOUBLE attempts remaining. Expiry while running overrides allowances; paused deadlines retain durations rather than falsely expiring during pause. Standalone negative trap scores versus embedded zero clamp remain distinct. This adds previously undefined explicit incorrect-attempt/DOUBLE/PHONE mechanics, subject to human gameplay acceptance.

#### Correction, VAR and results

Immediate UNDO_EFFECT is latest reversible gameplay effect only, before another effect/transition/FINISH, including NO_SCORE. Reverse recorded actual deltas once (clamped−50 reverses+50, not nominal−200), retain disclosure/aids/clocks. Ruling undo enters correction review, not fresh timed guessing. Timing/information effects cannot be undone; stealing compensation does not refund consumption.

CORRECT_RULING also preserves access to earlier completed own tiles: unfinished BOARD/no unresolved active question; exact current adjudication/correction event ID/version, expected game version, replacement ruling/eligible team set and bounded reason. Lock correction chain/teams; resolve retry; compute replacement from pinned rules and original bonus snapshot; append compensating postings/correction event; update current ruling/scores, preserving completion/turn/clocks/disclosed answers/aid consumption. NO_SCORE/shared-correct/bonus cases supported; cannot retrospectively buy/move a bonus.

Every effect records source events and score reads. Permit earlier correction when subsequent affected-team postings are fixed additive amounts independent of changed balances and resulting mode constraints remain valid. Reject CORRECTION_DEPENDENCY_REVIEW_REQUIRED for descendants using changed ranking, cap/clamp, derived amounts or dependent results; never silently recompute opponent choices/unrelated actions. Offer owner VAR report linking proposed correction/blocking events. VAR is bounded pinned-question/event reporting, no score/content mutation. Administrative resolution needs separately reviewed scoped authority, not generic score editing.

FINISHED runtime stays immutable. Post-final correction requires append-only result version/predecessor hash and separately authorized role; otherwise report-only/deny mutation. INT-063 validates authoritative versions/downstream correction blocking. Optional tie lottery samples once among tied leaders, stores draw/outcome, leaves scores unchanged and clearly publishes LOTTERY result evidence; retry never redraws. Tournament lottery use remains gated by owner-approved tie policy.

**Checks/rollback:** Every aid and permitted/rejected pairing, deadlines/competing calls, attempts/shared awards, duplicate consumption/reversal, NO_SCORE/bonus/clamp/dependency corrections, reload/privacy/foreign IDs/stale grants, terminal denial and fixed lottery replay; narrow source/API/UI tests, exact SQL/TS proof/real restricted races later, actual responsive controls and human gameplay separate. Disable new successor effects/starts on rollback while preserving compatible active matches, pins/postings/consumption/result history and ledger. **Status:** Source planning adopted; E2/061 and domain prerequisite review pending, no062implementation yet. No SQL/native/cloud/receipt activation. Assignment estimate later; telemetry unavailable.

**Authorities and fixed decisions (INT-D01–D09).** D01: Huroof owns shell, routes, Firebase games and existing immutable Huroof content; Enta's imported service owns relational quiz, study, tournament and business operations; shared API contract and same-origin routing bridge them. D02: Firebase UID from the new project uniquely identifies a PostgreSQL user; Express verifies that project's ID tokens; no shared-code/JWT login remains in the combined app. D03: guests may join Huroof; verified email or Google accounts may host, claim one lifetime free credit and buy credits. Enta remains host-operated on a shared screen; only bounded, revocable match-scoped judge/actor QR access is added. D04: one credit is consumed per successfully started hosted match in either engine, including rematches and played tournament matches. Huroof internal rounds, tournament setup/byes, joining and individual study are free. Client-provided game mode is never an entitlement authority. D05: PostgreSQL owns immutable wallet ledger, holds, commerce and reconciliation; Firestore owns durable Huroof admission state. D06: one canonical category can map to separate approved, immutable source-specific content/media revisions, with mode/tier availability; active matches pin those revisions. D07: production payment requires a configured live merchant and stored order snapshot; no deploy-time seed or silent mock gateway. D08: exactly three screenshot-backed brand concepts, immutable evidence and explicit human selection precede visual implementation; homepage human live review precedes visual expansion. Historical `DESIGN-DNA.md` remains binding until the new approved direction supersedes it. D09: stop new old-system starts and checkouts only during the staged cutover; drain existing rooms and maintain settlement callbacks/support until obligations clear. Rollback retains the new ledger and never restores an older database over new payments.

**State and boundary contract to finish in INT-1.** A reservation is unique for `(host Firebase UID, engine, logical match ID, request key)` and bound to project, request hash and wallet account. Huroof holds remain pending until Firestore durably records either `STARTED` or permanent `CANCELLED`; `START_MATCH` and cancellation must compete in the same Firestore transaction. A started record commits the PostgreSQL debit idempotently. A hold is released only after Firestore confirms cancellation; an unavailable service leaves it pending for reconciliation. Invalid/stale starts cost nothing. Enta creates its authoritative started match and debit in one PostgreSQL transaction. Purchase and grant idempotency keys, order snapshot, exact currency minor units, refunds, chargebacks and admin adjustments require auditable records. These are invariant requirements, not a claim that current code implements them.

**Service/role/content boundaries.** Public catalog returns only published availability and safe descriptions, never drafts, grading keys or unrevealed answers. Host, Huroof guest player, audience, Enta judge, Enta actor and admin each get an explicit capability matrix; nested resources must be bound to the authorized parent match/account. Every advertised game mode and tier must have a reviewed, rights-cleared, decodable supply manifest sufficient for a fresh and repeat match. Content edits create successors; retirement cannot mutate pinned active/history records. Source answer/media authority remains with its own engine. The exact API namespaces, compatibility versioning, deployment and additive database migration sequence are INT-1 deliverables.

## T-11 — Required join names and host-created manual players (2026-09-08)

**Milestone:** M-10. **Owner:** Forge implementation/checks; root acceptance with database/security boundary review before implementation and material-risk Gate before final acceptance. **Status:** Done — root accepted with technical Gate PASS 2026-09-08. **Authorization:** user requests a required join name and host creation of named players without devices/buzzers, coexisting with joined device players. Add only; no removal or new management product.

### Source evidence and design decisions

Current source: EntryRoute sends `name.trim() || 'لاعب'` to both join paths; server/service.join also defaults to `لاعب`. Firebase joinRoom calls validateDisplayName with that fallback before checking existing membership. Its existing validator trims, bounds at 48 UTF-16 code units and rejects control characters. Firebase CanonicalMember UID is an auth identity: index.writes creates `player_<uid>` projections, and firestore.rules authenticates membership using request.auth.uid. Therefore inserting manual entries as members with fabricated UID would incorrectly mix roster and credentials. T-08–10 supply host roster, UID-safe capsules and team moves; T-10/M-9 is accepted, with the later lobby correction and outstanding user visual review preserved as dated evidence. T-09/M-8 was separately accepted by its owning task. Current allReady uses active device players and existing team/ready checks; index.joinRoom caps device players at 16, and team allocation reads members. These must consider manual participants without treating them as sessions.

**D-11.1 — Canonical separate roster:** add optional `manualParticipants?: Array<{ id: string; displayName: string; team: TeamAxis }>` to canonical room JSON in local authority and Firebase. Missing means empty. IDs are server-created UUIDs independent of auth UID; no token, capability, Auth user, member document, player projection or self identity is ever created. This additive room field is necessary to persist the explicitly requested non-device participants; no SQL table, Firestore collection, migration/backfill, indexes or rules change is needed. Existing members remain device participants by default. Retain participants across existing room lifecycle just like the current member roster.

**D-11.2 — Safe presentation and targeting:** project manual participants into the existing displayed player roster with `participation: 'manual'`, displayName/team and derived `ready: true`. Give only host projections `manualParticipantId`; never put manual IDs into `uid`. Existing/omitted participation is device. Public/player summaries may display the truthful name/team/type but no target identifier or private answers. Use discriminated capsule targets internally: device memberUid or manualParticipantId. Extend existing LOBBY_ASSIGN_TEAM payload validation to accept exactly one identifier plus valid team; reject both/neither/extra keys. Existing device payload remains compatible. Resolve IDs only in the corresponding collection. Manual moves keep derived readiness; device lobby moves still clear readiness. UID-based device authorization and self remain unchanged.

**D-11.3 — Host addition:** new host-only intent `LOBBY_ADD_MANUAL_PLAYER` with exact `{displayName, team}`. Trim/validate the name and team at authority; generate unique ID server-side only after revision/role/state/capacity validation. Firebase pure reducer accepts an authority-generated ID input for addition, or a narrowly scoped server-owned factory; clients cannot choose it. Replayed intent uses existing receipt and cannot create a second participant; transaction retries never persist duplicates. Permit addition in LOBBY only for this minimum requested feature, with visible reason elsewhere; existing safe between-question team-move states remain unchanged. User has requested creation, not late joining of manual participants. Add/remove/rename/convert-to-device flows beyond creation are excluded.

**D-11.4 — Combined roster semantics:** total active players = active device players plus manual entries. Both authorities cap this combined total at existing MAX_PLAYERS=16; use combined team sizes for new device auto-allocation. Preserve zero-player start behavior. With any participants, require at least two total and one on each valid team, every device participant ready, and every manual participant assigned (required at creation). All-manual and mixed starts work; adding manual participants does not mark devices ready. Lobby counts/ready counts reflect participants, not connections, and names may duplicate. Manual players never issue LOBBY_SET_READY or BUZZ; those operations still require the genuine authenticated/capability player actor. Existing HOST_SELECT_TEAM supplies manual answer selection, also in mixed rooms. Compute any UI `hostOnly`/device-buzzer messaging from device participants where appropriate so all-manual rooms retain the manual answer controls. Do not change buzzer eligibility, phase transitions, scoring, board, deadlines or winner history.

**D-11.5 — Mandatory device join name:** new joins require a string that trims to 1–48 UTF-16 code units and has no Unicode control characters, matching the existing Firebase bound. Reject missing, whitespace-only, non-string, overlong and control-character input at EntryRoute, local service/HTTP boundary and Firebase callable; never silently substitute `لاعب` or truncate. Allow real Arabic and duplicate names. Preserve separate host/audience defaults. Firebase checks an existing authenticated active membership before requiring a new-join name, retaining prior closed-room policy and reconnect identity/name; do not revalidate or rename legacy members on reconnect. Local reconnect already uses an issued capability rather than a new join: preserve that path, never match by display name. Join adapters must propagate useful Arabic validation feedback rather than collapsing every rejection into “room not found.”

## T-12 — Truthful host player connection status (2026-09-08)

**Milestone:** M-11. **Owner:** Forge implementation/checks; root scope/acceptance, with security/database disposition before storage/boundary implementation and material-risk Gate before Done. **Status:** Done — root accepted with technical Gate PASS; broader suite timeout retained below. **Authorization:** user requests seeing which players are currently connected. This authorizes bounded additive presence storage, not production deployment, new RTDB setup or changing game readiness/scoring. T-11/M-10 is accepted; preserve its later room-before-name entry flow and bottom display-tab shortcut. Earlier T-09–10 status remains unchanged.

### Current evidence

`HostPlayerCapsule` in GameRoutes.tsx (around 1015–1060) currently renders ✓ for member.ready and بدون بازر for manual participants; readiness is not connection. `server/index.ts` stores per-room WebSocket sets containing ws/token, sends game metadata on connect/action/tick, and simply deletes the socket on close. It has no per-player reference aggregation or ping/pong liveness. `useRoom` in GameRoutes (around 733+) currently receives local game envelopes and Firebase subscribeProjection callbacks, sets connection from received data and drives automatic actions by game revision. Separate presence must not be mistaken for a game envelope or trigger those effects. Inspected current source has no explicit same-revision rejection there, but this is not a reason to embed heartbeat state in game projections.

Firebase adapter uses authenticated callable functions and onSnapshot game projections; there is no presence service. DeferredFirebaseGameAdapter must forward any new optional methods while retaining lazy loading. Firebase canonical members are auth-bearing; manual participants are a separate canonical room array. Host display is an audience projection opened under an existing identity: neither route label nor requested projection role is authority for player presence. `graphify affected server/index.ts` returned no affected nodes and warned of skill/package version mismatch, so source inspection, not graph completeness, governs this plan.

### Decisions and smallest implementation

**D-12.1 — Meaning:** a device player is connected when at least one authenticated participant transport/session for that room and canonical player UID is currently live according to the authority. This means the game client is communicating, not a claim that a person is watching or that the device is ready. Canonical active membership is only authorization/roster membership. Manual participants have no connection state: keep بدون بازر. Presence never changes ready, team eligibility, start rules, score, timer, audit or game revision.

**D-12.2 — Independent channel:** define a HostPresenceSnapshot with roomId, serverTime, observed device-player IDs and per-player connected/lastSeen/lease expiry as applicable; include a separate freshness status on the client. Keep it outside ProjectionEnvelope and independent of game revision. Local WebSocket sends tagged `{type:'presence', ...}` messages to canonical host sockets only, routed before the game-envelope handler; it retains the existing game transport instead of creating a duplicate local socket. Firebase gets optional runtime adapter methods `subscribeHostPresence` and `startPlayerPresence` (names may follow existing naming convention), forwarded through deferred adapter. Firebase subscribeHostPresence may internally poll authenticated callable reads rather than establish a Firestore listener. Fixture/unsupported channels show unknown. A small useRoomPresence hook owns state/cleanup; avoid a routing refactor.

**D-12.3 — Local authority:** authenticate upgrade once using capability verification and existing canonical member lookup; store immutable roomId/UID/actual role alongside socket. Count only canonical player members, never manual IDs, host or audience. Maintain per-room/per-UID live socket refs. On open/close/termination, send fresh host presence snapshots without game metadata writes/revision increments. Ping every 15s; record pong, terminate a socket whose last authenticated liveness exceeds 45s, and aggregate online while any socket remains. Send a server-timestamped host presence snapshot at least every 15s even if unchanged so a stalled host stream expires truthfully. Clean refs/maps/timers on close and process shutdown. Local normal close can update host immediately; abrupt network loss is detected within 45–60s, including sweep scheduling. Ping/pong transport liveness does not imply foreground visibility.

**D-12.4 — Firebase UID leases, existing infrastructure only:** use private server-owned per-device documents at `rooms/{roomId}/presence/{uid}`, separate from canonical room, members, projections, events and intent receipts. Store one lease document per actual device UID with minimal server-owned uid, updatedAt and expiresAtMs. Per-UID documents avoid shared-document transaction contention; host reads are bounded to the current active device roster (maximum16). Missing document or never-observed UID means unknown, not disconnected. Authenticated renewPresence accepts exact `{roomId}`, verifies active canonical player membership and room availability, and derives UID from request.auth and times from the server clock. Client sends no UID/session ID/role/online/timestamp. Heartbeat immediately and every15s while a genuine player client is mounted; TTL45s. Throttle persisted renewals transactionally to at most once per15s per UID, so multiple tabs share one lease and cannot amplify writes. Do not issue offline/release writes on unmount: one tab closing must never clear another tab's connection. Last-tab disappearance becomes offline after the final lease expires. Local refs still support immediate normal-close detection. Cancel timers/retries on teardown, avoid overlapping requests and refresh on foreground/online recovery. Manual/host/audience actors cannot renew as players.

**D-12.5 — Host callable read instead of new Firestore rules:** authenticated host-only getRoomPresence is polled immediately and every10s while the host view is mounted, returning derived status against server time. It rechecks canonical host membership, filters current real device players and returns no credential or session artifacts. Known unexpired lease means connected, known expired lease means disconnected, and never-seen lease means unknown. Preserve the expired observation for this distinction; read only known current roster UID document paths rather than listing arbitrary presence entries. Do not refresh lease timestamps when reading. A separate listener-readable Firestore projection adds rules/cache plumbing; do not add it or RTDB. Private documents remain denied by existing catch-all rules. No scheduled TTL job is required; missing/old data remains safe and ignored outside the current device roster. Root database/security review must approve this UID-only callable polling design before implementation.
**D-12.6 — Freshness and limits:** host initializes unknown (`حالة الاتصال غير معروفة`), never defaults to green. Successful authoritative snapshot establishes a server-time anchor against monotonic client time; detect expiry from elapsed time rather than trusting device wall clock. Host unknown overrides all device dots immediately on detected offline/transport failure/cache-only or subscription failure; also after 30s without a successful authoritative presence snapshot, on foreground resume until refresh, and when the runtime cannot supply presence. Fresh snapshots may label connected or غير متصل. Firebase status delivery adds up to10s poll delay; last-tab or abrupt player failure can remain connected for up to55s (45s lease plus poll), communicated as approximately one minute, excluding service/network delay which must result in unknown at the host. Background suspension can expire a device lease even though a tab still exists; it becomes connected again when communication resumes. Document this as recent communication, not physical network truth. Status need not equal local WebSocket's exact instant, but both runtimes implement the same user meaning and unknown behavior.

**D-12.7 — UI:** device capsules show a small dot with readable متصل / غير متصل or unknown text, using UID lookup only. Duplicate names remain independent. Readiness is distinct, lobby-only labelled جاهز / بانتظار الجاهزية; never relabel ✓ as online. Manual badges remain بدون بازر, with no dot. Preserve capsule drag/tap/keyboard assignment, compact T-10 cards, fixed axes, QR/name flow, Add manual form and bottom display shortcut. Connection state does not disable assignment/start beyond existing rules.

### VISUAL CONTRACT — copy verbatim for implementation

Mood/concept: preserve approved مدار الحروف, corrected navy lobby/live host cards and existing manual capsule treatment; presence is a compact factual annotation.
Focal/scan order: player name first, device connection status second; lobby readiness remains a separate secondary status. Board/question, rounds/points hierarchy and established host action order stay unchanged.
Density: host5/lobby4; one small dot plus short readable text per device capsule, natural wrapping for long names; no new panel or status dashboard.
Desktop/mobile: preserve paired green-left/red-right cards and 320px+ no-overflow behavior, 44px capsule targets and keyboard/200% zoom operation. Keep bottom display shortcut and existing last operational actions.
Typography: IBM Plex Sans Arabic; readable compact 400–500 status text, existing name/action hierarchy; never shrink player names to make room. Arabic is untracked.
Palette/surfaces: existing token roles; connected uses existing semantic positive indication, disconnected/unknown neutral high-contrast dot/text, no new team identity color. Color never carries status alone.
Spacing/shapes: existing 4px scale and capsule radius; keep related status text close to its name with wrapping; edit scoped canonical CSS without override tails.
Icons/imagery: simple decorative status dot with textual متصل/غير متصل/unknown; manual players retain بدون بازر and no device dot. No new imagery or animated activity glyph.
Interaction/states: truthful unknown until fresh authority evidence; stale/offline host invalidates status, reconnect refreshes it. Lobby ready text is distinct from connection; assignment drag/tap/keyboard and manual creation remain unchanged. Presence cannot change gameplay readiness or legal actions.
Motion: static status changes, reduced motion static, no pulsing online dots or countdown animation.
Anti-patterns: never infer connected from ready/active, never show a manual player connected, no fake fresh green from cached data, no game-revision heartbeat, no public UID leakage, no new visual direction/board changes or status-only nested cards.

### Impact, rollback and unknowns

Private bounded lease storage is additive and ephemeral; no canonical room schema, migration or permissions expansion. Heartbeats/polls create callable/read/write traffic proportional to open game tabs; document 15s player heartbeat/10s host polling and measure emulator call counts to prevent duplicate-effect loops. Pause polling when unmounted; background resume refreshes immediately. Host read must not write game state. Deployment cost tuning/schedulers are outside this request.

Rollback removes only reviewed T-12 code hunks, preserving mixed user work and canonical rooms. Remaining private lease documents are inert/expired, not deleted; no data migration rollback required. Stop owned timers/listeners on teardown. Unknowns for T-12.1: exact existing canonical actor helper access, callable test setup, closed-room lease/read policy consistent with existing room availability, and host/client error plumbing. Root must record database/security disposition before implementation; no review or runtime success is claimed by planning.

**Root design/storage disposition (2026-09-08):** choose UID-only per-device private Firestore documents and host callable polling, superseding listener/session-map alternatives. Storage reviewed per-UID documents to avoid shared-document contention. Heartbeat15s, lease45s, transactionally accepted write at most once per15s per UID, host poll10s; approximately one-minute disconnect delay. Callables read room/member for auth/active/closed checks and write only the actor lease, never game/members/projections. Host-only polling returns sanitized current device roster data with server-time anchor. Existing catch-all rules deny the private path; no new browser rules or RTDB. Security confirmation of this final callable variant is pending root's recorded disposition; implementation remains behind that prerequisite.

**T-12.1 final boundary disposition (root, 2026-09-08):** Security confirms the final private per-UID lease plus host-only callable polling design has no blocker. Storage per-UID recommendation is incorporated. Implementation authorized; retain D-12 missing-lease unknown semantics (expired observed lease disconnected), exact payload/auth/active/open checks, transactional throttle, bounded roster reads and no game writes. Invocation/read-cost limiting is outside the timer throttle guarantee; preserve App Check. T-12.1 complete.

### VISUAL CONTRACT for T-14.2 — copy verbatim into the Forge handoff

Mood/concept: reuse approved مدار الحروف Arabic game studio and existing host/audience/player treatments; image questions are functional extensions of the current question surface.
Focal/scan order: current question image and prompt first, gameplay action/buzzer second, score/round context third; the host's answer remains in its existing private answer area.
Density:4–5 of10; one media panel with breathing room, no gallery or administration chrome in play.
Desktop/mobile: contained image preserving full aspect ratio beside/above the prompt on desktop and above it on320px+ mobile; never crop meaningful puzzle/lineup content; preserve touch controls and no horizontal overflow.
Typography: existing IBM Plex Sans Arabic roles and sizes; natural RTL text, no tracking, no text embedded into newly generated assets.
Palette/surfaces: current approved tokens, navy/cobalt surfaces and established semantic team colors; neutral media backdrop, no new aesthetic system.
Spacing/shapes: existing4px spacing scale, existing question-card radii and control sizing; image frame remains subordinate to the question.
Icons/imagery: use the actual verified240 assets only; neutral image labels that do not reveal answers; review sheets and redesign briefs never appear as playable images.
Interaction/states: accessible loading, loaded, failed/retry and unauthorized/hidden states; image visibility follows authoritative role/lifecycle/audience toggle; keyboard-accessible retry, polite error announcement, no automatic answer reveal.
Motion: no new image entrance animation; respect reduced motion and existing text reveal/pause behavior.
Anti-patterns: stretched/cropped puzzles, answer-bearing alt text/filenames, public permanent media tokens, fake placeholders presented as real assets, a new design direction, board/score/control redesign.

## Proposed product rules and decision register

These are proposed defaults for implementation planning, not claims of user selection where wording was ambiguous. Root should record durable D-15 IDs and resolve consequential deviations before implementation.

- **D-15.1 / game kind:** add `gameKind: huroof | categories`, independent of `mode: classic | fast | custom` (pace/setup preset) and `modality: classic | image | charades` (question presentation). Missing gameKind in legacy rooms reads as huroof. Avoid overloading classic. First category delivery supports classic question presentation; image is enabled only after T-14.2 media parity and explicit supported-combination tests. Charades remains its separate existing flow; do not silently feed it to category or letter boards. Lock kind and category scope when creating a room; rematch copies settings into a new match. The existing classic/fast/custom timing truth remains unless separately changed.
- **D-15.2 / numbered category labels:** category mode keeps the exact 25-cell topology and team connection win condition. Cells show selected category + a per-category occurrence number, e.g. `كرة القدم [1]`, `الفن [2]`, `كرة القدم [2]`. Number means a unique visible occurrence for that category within the round, not points, difficulty, question ID or board coordinate. Keep immutable coordinate cellId and store categoryId/label/occurrence separately. Allocate initial occurrences deterministically in board coordinate order; later replacement gets the next unused number for its new category, never renumber other cells or reuse a label in the same round. Reset counters on a new round. Show a short “الرقم لتمييز خلايا الفئة” hint in rules/setup. Category names must actually be on cells, with line wrapping and full accessible names.
- **D-15.3 / initial category distribution:** at least two distinct playable selected categories are required to promise a genuinely different category on failure. Allocate 25 slots evenly across eligible selections (difference at most one where capacity permits), seed/shuffle positions server-side. Selected catalog presence is not playable capacity: only approved/pinned release questions and distinct unused concepts count. If a selected category cannot support its allocated cells/reserves, show exact coverage guidance before room creation, rather than borrowing an unselected category. Decide a supported maximum (reuse current maximum ten unless category-label evidence requires less).
- **D-15.4 / wrong versus terminal:** initial JUDGE_INCORRECT grants the other team its existing opportunity on the same question; do not rotate then. Opponent incorrect, opponent-window timeout, or no buzz during the initial window resolves the question as failed. FIRST_ANSWER currently stops its clock and waits for the host judgment; retain that unless a separate answer timer is explicitly designed. Pause, disconnection and reload are not question failures. Stale/replayed judgment must have no extra consequence.
- **D-15.5 / terminal replacement:** on a terminal failure, close buzzing, consume the question/concept, record one resolution event, and keep the cell unowned with no score. Retain the failed question/answer in a bounded result presentation until the host chooses Continue; at that point atomically commit replacement and return to CELL_SELECTION. “Retry” must never reopen that disclosed question. Category cells change to another eligible selected category; numbered Huroof surprise cells retain their stable 1–9 tile number and rotate to a different eligible letter. For Huroof show the number as identity and the current revealed letter as the main value; on return the number can become primary again until selection, but the letter replacement must persist server-side. Existing ordinary letter cells keep their letter and draw a fresh question on the next visit. This interpretation avoids extending the user's numbered-cell request to every visible letter.
- **D-15.6 / pool depletion:** do not repeat a consumed question or answer concept, silently widen category scope, select unavailable content or pretend replacement occurred. Require a different eligible category/letter; if none exists, put the match into an explicit content-exhausted hold, with no owner/score mutation and an explanation to the host. Do not disable the cell and continue silently, as that could make connection victory impossible. Offer a reviewed end-without-winner or new-match action; keep room state recoverable. Content exhaustion is distinct from timer/no-answer failure. Select/replacement commit must include reservation/consumption atomically so concurrency cannot oversubscribe reserves. Finite pools cannot guarantee unlimited failures; startup coverage must say what it guarantees. Preserve release pinning through rounds and reconnection; no live release swap to evade depletion.
- **D-15.7 / privacy and compatibility:** public projections may expose current category/occurrence and current revealed letter, never next hidden replacement content, accepted answers, sources, moderation or queues. Keep old schema rooms playable under their versioned policy or reject unsupported new clients explicitly; no destructive migration of live rooms. New rules require a room policy/schema discriminator. Corrections alter ownership/outcomes under existing audit rules; they do not rewind consumed questions or secretly restore previous labels.

## Compact visual contract — carry verbatim in the implementation handoff

Mood/concept: preserve human-approved مدار الحروف for استوديو الحروف, a cobalt architectural Arabic game studio with raised ice-white real board cells and calm readable task surfaces; immutable 0007 supersedes stale flat clauses in DESIGN-DNA. Focal/scan: entry current joining/creating decision then CTA; lobby code/share then roster/readiness then Start; host board/current question/timer then moderation console; player instruction then tactile buzzer; audience board/question/timer with green physically left and red physically right; admin title/status then filters, records and bounded editor actions. Density: entry/lobby4, setup/host5, audience/player3, admin6. Composition: desktop max1200px task shell, two-column setup and two-team lobby, frontal live board with fixed side scores, 16:9 audience safe stage; mobile one-column entry/lobby with reachable CTA, compact scores above board, one-thumb player, contained table overflow only for admin. Typography: IBM Plex Sans Arabic700 display/letters/scores,600 actions/headings,400–500 body; no Arabic tracking, phone body16px, tabular scores, bidi-isolated room codes/numbers. Palette/surfaces: approved --spatial-* cobalt/ultramarine, deep-blue ink, opaque ice-white zones, cyan focus/action; crimson/emerald remain team semantics; decorative background stays outside text zones. Spacing/shapes: existing4px scale,24–64px section rhythm,44px targets,12px controls and16–20px principal panels, restrained shadows and no nested-card clutter. Imagery/icons: approved spatial WebPs, authentic DOM/SVG board and rights-cleared category covers with fallbacks; one labelled outline family; category names plus occurrence numbers remain readable in actual cells. Interaction: rest/focus/pressed/busy/disabled reason/error/empty/stale/offline/reconnect/success explicit; legal server actions and truthful permissions unchanged. Motion:100ms press,200ms state, finite600–800ms entry only where useful, finite existing near-win/win feedback, short replacement transition keyed to authoritative resolution revision, static reduced-motion and no replay on reconnect. Anti-patterns: no new brand/concept, no neon/glass/rainbow/gold, no ambient loops, no moving live targets, no mirrored board geometry, no fake players/metrics/content, no screenshots baked into controls, no tiny long category labels, no auth bypass or technical publication promises.

### Proposed consequential delta — M44.6-O5-S-REENTRY.RE2.CONTAIN — 2026-10-06

Astra medium read-only replanning establishes that current worker-local polling cannot guarantee surviving caller return plus confirmed drain when its compiler worker or native descendant stops responding. Installed esbuild main.js line2434 waits without timeout; parent callbacks cannot run during that wait. Current HeldWindow.close bounds a termination attempt but swallows termination failure; that is not confirmed successful drain. Current RE2–RE3 remains unadmitted. No operational trial or budget exception follows from this proposal.

Root selects developing the process-containment design for review, while existing exact30 resolution-metadata repair continues independently. Architecture/implementation adoption remains conditional on fresh Database/Security concurrence and resolution of D4/D5 below. This entry authorizes only read-only contract/feasibility inventory at present.

Decision register:
- CONTAIN-D1 (proposed): a narrowly exposed owned native Windows adapter in the existing Node process owns a private Job Object and launches compiler brokers suspended; no outer publisher launcher/classifier exception.
- CONTAIN-D2 (proposed): intercept only the source-pinned esbuild compiler constructor/request boundary; installed dependencies, four commands and native service protocol remain unchanged.
- CONTAIN-D3 (binding constraint): existing96-byte phase and16-byte control SABs remain main-owned within the existing process. Never claim SABs cross processes. Broker-local buffers/channels have explicitly different provenance and no phase/readiness/credential/publication authority.
- CONTAIN-D4 (unresolved): identify an existing finite operation deadline for every post-READY compilation and bind it without renewal. Requests lacking one cannot enter an admitted route. No generic newly invented compiler timeout.
- CONTAIN-D5 (unresolved): identify and allocate an existing cleanup allowance to job termination and exit confirmation. Existing monitor two-stage waits do not automatically authorize an extra compiler allowance.
- CONTAIN-D6 (explicit assurance limit): surviving Node/native owner, Windows scheduler and kernel remain functioning. Failed query, unknown or unconfirmed exit remains INCOMPLETE; no universal kernel/observer/hostile-same-user proof.

Surviving refusal boundary: the current owned wrapper retains esbuild's original reply endpoint and original8-byte notification buffer. An isolated broker within the job creates the pinned compiler worker with the existing3 workerData keys and broker-local SAB/MessageChannel; results traverse a new owned private transport. Parent waits in finite native polling slices, returning to JS to check inherited deadlines and both original controls. Queue exactly one matching resolve/reject/properties reply through the retained original endpoint BEFORE setting/notifying original buffer, then return from postMessage; installed SDK wait is already satisfied. A broken original endpoint throws before entering the installed wait. Actual argument/result/error types must survive; plain JSON silent type loss is forbidden and nonrepresentable input refuses before dispatch. One native registry owns the job across main/monitor threads; endpoints bind run, requesting thread, instance and sequentialID. Fatal compiler failure makes the job terminal, with no automatic broker replacement/retry. Parent return alone is not confirmed drain.

Windows ownership and exit contract (primary sources supplied by Astra): private unnamed noninheritable JobObject, KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, neither breakaway allowance; minimal explicit inherited-handle list excludes job-owner handle, publication locks/credentials/unrelated handles. Create pinned broker executable suspended with fixed environment/cwd/args; assign and confirm membership BEFORE primary-thread resume. Assignment/nested-job incompatibility refuses without breakaway retry. Close dispatch and terminate only the owned job on failure; confirm broker process handle/creation identity exit and zero active job membership before clean completion. Completion events supplement authoritative handle/accounting checks; lost notifications do not establish exit. Do not use WaitForSingleObject(job) as generic all-child-exit proof. Ordinary CreateProcess descendant membership is insufficient for alternate creation mechanisms such as WMI; admitted executables must exclude those routes. Successful TerminateJobObject/TerminateProcess calls do not confirm drain; pending IO or failed/late queries remain INCOMPLETE, and forced termination does not guarantee DLL cleanup.

Primary references: [Job Objects](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/procthread/job-objects), [creation flags](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/procthread/process-creation-flags), [assignment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/jobapi2/nf-jobapi2-assignprocesstojobobject), [handle list](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-updateprocthreadattribute), [job termination](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/jobapi2/nf-jobapi2-terminatejobobject), [job accounting](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winnt/ns-winnt-jobobject_basic_accounting_information), [termination semantics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-terminateprocess).
